newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico mulls plan to boost maquiladora suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico mulls plan to boost maquiladora suppliers.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned development banks will announce a plan shortly to help develop a national supplier base for the booming maquiladora, or in-bond, sector, officials say.
Development bank Nacional Financiera and export-import bank Bancomext will launch a pilot project within a month or two in the northern industrial corridor near the Mexico-U.S. border.

"We are studying a program for suppliers of the maquilas, we want to do it together with Bancomext ... each focusing on their own niche," associate finance director of Nacional Financiera (Nafin) Federico Patino told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
Nafin is looking at electrical goods and automotive companies in the border area for the pilot project, he said.
"We have already talked to four or five companies that are interested in participating in the program. We should decide which ones soon," he said.
Many in-bond factories in northern Mexico import supplies in order to add value and re-export them.
Patino said he estimates between $30 and $35 billion worth of maquiladora industry supplies are used each year -- but only about two percent are produced in Mexico.

He said rules of origin under the North American Free Trade Agreement would force some maquiladora companies to begin paying a tax on raw materials imported from outside the NAFTA region beginning in 2001.
"That is why it is important for maquiladora companies who do not have a supplier in the region to set one up in Mexico," Patino said.
